module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 16

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/16](https://www.erdosproblems.com/16)
- [Ch23] Chen, Yong-Gao, A conjecture of Erdős on $p+2^k$. arXiv:2312.04120 (2023).
- [Er50] Erdős, P., On integers of the form $2^k+p$ and some related problems. Summa Brasil. Math.
  (1950), 113-123.
- [Ro34] Romanoff, N. P., Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie. Math. Ann. (1934), 668-678.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Nat Filter Set
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos16

/--
The set of odd integers not of the form $2^k+p$.
-/
def Erdos16Set : Set ℕ :=
  { n | Odd n ∧ ¬ ∃ k p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ n = 2 ^ k + p }

/--
A set of natural numbers has density 0.
-/
def density_zero (S : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  open scoped Classical in
  Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦ (count (· ∈ S) x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 0)

/--
Is the set of odd integers not of the form $2^k+p$ the union of an infinite arithmetic progression
and a set of density $0$?

Erdős called this conjecture "rather silly".

Chen [Ch23] has proved the answer is no.

This was formalized in Lean by Chin using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/danielchin/proofs/blob/main/Proofs/ErdosProblems/Erdos16.lean"]
theorem erdos_16 :
    answer(False) ↔
      ∃ A B : Set ℕ, Erdos16Set = A ∪ B ∧
        (∃ a d : ℕ, d > 0 ∧ A = { x | ∃ m : ℕ, x = a + m * d }) ∧
        density_zero B := by
  sorry

/--
A set of natural numbers has positive lower density.
-/
def positive_lower_density (S : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  open scoped Classical in
  0 < atTop.liminf (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((count (· ∈ S) n : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) : EReal))

/--
Romanoff [Ro34] showed that the set of odd integers of this form has positive density.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_16.variant.romanoff :
    let S := { n : ℕ | Odd n ∧ ∃ k p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ n = 2 ^ k + p }
    positive_lower_density S := by
  sorry

/--
Using covering congruences Erdős [Er50] proved that the set of odd integers which are not of this
form contains an infinite arithmetic progression.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_16.variant.erdos :
    ∃ a d : ℕ, d > 0 ∧ { x | ∃ m : ℕ, x = a + m * d } ⊆ Erdos16Set := by
  sorry

end Erdos16

reformulations.difference: Lean allows k = 0, whereas Chen's §1 defines the corresponding set using positive exponents. Consequently Chen's set includes 3, while Erdos16Set does not.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An odd number represented with exponent zero must be 1 + 2 = 3, since every other prime is odd. Thus Chen's set is exactly Erdos16Set ∪ {3}. This difference does not affect any of the three theorem statements: positive lower density is invariant under finite changes; an infinite AP can be replaced by a tail avoiding 3; and in an AP-plus-density-zero decomposition, the discarded finite initial segment can be absorbed into the density-zero remainder. The set equality and the equivalences for all three uses were proved in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean and /workspace/review/density-invariance.lean.

reformulations.difference: The source's phrase 'positive density' is formalized as strictly positive lower density, without asserting that an ordinary asymptotic-density limit exists.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Romanoff's original p. 668, footnote 1, defines positive density by N(x)/x > α for all sufficiently large x, for some α > 0. This is equivalent to a positive liminf, not to existence of a positive density limit. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, positive_lower_density was proved equivalent to existence of a positive eventual lower bound on the counting ratios. Strict versus non-strict bounds are interchangeable by decreasing the positive constant; counting below x versus through x changes the numerator by at most one.

review.notes: Checked all three definitions and all three theorems, including zero/empty cases, small representability examples, count normalization, answer polarity, and infinitude of the AP when d > 0. Both density definitions have the intended semantics. The source records the main problem as disproved with a Lean proof, agreeing with research solved and answer(False). The linked proof uses the weaker remainder condition 'contains no infinite AP', so its negative conclusion is stronger than needed. I compiled that proof and supplied a bridge to the exact reviewed statement in /workspace/review/full-proof-check.lean; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
